requirements_summary: Workload: low-latency decisioning for bidding + personalization (short prompts, median 12 tokens).
Latency/throughput targets: p50 < 25ms, p95 < 110ms; sustained 800 req/s; burst up to 2k req/s with graceful degradations.
Cost sensitivity: high — target blended cost < $0.006 per 1k tokens at scale (rough target for fiscal modeling).
Model preferences: prefers open models (Llama2-13B, Mistral variants) with 4-bit quantization; fallback to smaller 7B models for non-critical routes.
Routing/fallback: route by latency SLO, model cost profile; automatic fallback to quantized variants when Dedicated pool near capacity.
Batching/caching needs: micro-batching to preserve tail latency, prefix/KV cache for repeated templates, suggest adaptive batch sizing.
Benchmarking ask: deliver matrix showing p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens across configs and sequence lengths.
Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, SOC2 compliance proof, KMS with key residency in EU, detailed audit logs for model inputs/outputs.
poc_acceptance_criteria: Meets p95 < 110ms on sustained 800 rps in the dedicated cluster test.
Demonstrated 20-35% cost reduction via quantization + caching vs. baseline fp16 config.
Seamless failover to fallback model under 15s with no dropped requests observed during simulated zone-failure test.
Security sign-off on KMS integration and audit log exports.
Operational runbook for autoscaling thresholds and batching parameters delivered.
recent_findings: 4-bit quantized 13B reduces token cost by ~28% but increases p95 by ~12-18ms without caching.
KV prefix cache cut p95 by ~40% on the top 300 prefixes in synthetic replay test.
Micro-batching (max batch 6-8) preserves p50 while smoothing throughput; larger batches harm p95 during bursts.
Fallback routing works but needs faster instance spin-up to meet their <15s failover SLA.
